summary:
H.R. 8884, the "Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act," amends title II of the Social Security Act to reauthorize and modify the Commissioner of Social Security's authority to conduct experiments and demonstration projects under section 234 (42 U.S.C. 434) relating to the disability insurance program. The text summarized is the version reported with an amendment (which struck all after the enacting clause and substituted new text) and referred to the Committee of the Whole.

Section 2(a) amends section 234(d)(2) to extend the authority to initiate demonstration projects from the expired December 31, 2021 date to December 31, 2030, and to extend the termination date for carrying out such projects from December 31, 2022 to December 31, 2031.

Section 2(b) amends section 234(c) (the authority to waive compliance with benefits requirements) by conforming the operative date to December 31, 2030; by extending the advance-notice period to Congress from 90 days to 120 days; and by adding a requirement that the report to Congress include the "evaluation metrics to be used" with respect to the experiment or demonstration project.

Section 2(c) revises section 201(k) (42 U.S.C. 401(k)) in its entirety, providing that administrative expenditures for section 234 experiments and demonstration projects be paid from funds made available for administration of title II, and that benefits payable by reason of participation be paid from either the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund or the Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund, as the Commissioner determines appropriate.

Section 2(d) amends section 234(e) to add a new paragraph (4), imposing a limitation that a participating individual's total income will not be reduced due to participation in an experiment or demonstration project, with conforming punctuation changes to paragraphs (2) and (3).

Section 2(e) makes technical amendments: in subsection (d)(1), substituting "section" for "subsection," and striking subsection (f) in its entirety.

Section 2(f) provides that the amendments made by section 2 take effect on January 1, 2027.

The bill operates as a reauthorization and amendment of existing demonstration authority rather than a new appropriation; funding is drawn from existing administrative appropriations and the specified trust funds. The extension effectively revives lapsed authority (which expired in 2021–2022) prospectively.
